headline: US midterms days away with election intimidation fears rising, markets sold off last night on NASDAQ tech weakness, and the Roosters edged the Knights 19-18 in the NRL Grand Final.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS dropped another 4% today — a brutal session for lithium. No specific news catalyst, but lithium prices remain depressed globally and sentiment toward the sector is weak. Down over 60% from your entry price, the long-term thesis depends on an EV demand recovery that hasn't arrived yet.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI fell 2.8% today on the ASX, dragged down by weakness in global AI and tech stocks — Alphabet and Microsoft both had rough sessions last night in the US, and that sentiment carried into this ETF today.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped 1.7% last night in what was a broad tech sell-off on the NASDAQ. No specific company news — it moved with the market. The long-term GTA VI release thesis is unchanged.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft fell 1.6% last night despite reporting quarterly earnings. The FY27 Q1 results are out and analysts are grading them — initial market reaction was muted to negative, suggesting results were solid but not a blowout. Long-term cloud and AI story remains intact.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Alphabet sank 1.45% last night after Q3 earnings disappointed the market enough to drag the NASDAQ lower. One analyst note suggests GOOG is a buy below $300, so at $278 it's now in that zone — but the earnings story is described as a 'horror show' continuing.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE fell 1.2% today, reflecting continued pressure on emerging markets. Rising oil prices and US election uncertainty tend to weigh on emerging market sentiment — nothing stock-specific here.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS dipped 0.7% today on the ASX, mirroring last night's US market weakness. The fund tracks the entire US sharemarket, so a soft NASDAQ night flows through here. Still sitting at a small profit overall.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG edged down 0.25% today — barely a move. Its diversification across global and Australian assets cushioned the US tech selloff nicely. Nothing to worry about here.

movers.name: DHHF
movers.note: DHHF slipped just 0.2% today — essentially flat. The broad diversified ETF held up well in a mixed market session. No news specific to the fund.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Earnings dip puts it in 'buy zone' — but hold for now
watch_today.detail: Alphabet fell 1.45% last night after Q3 results disappointed. At $278, it's below the $300 level some analysts call a buy zone. For a long-term holder, the ad revenue and AI business are still intact — this looks like a hold, and potentially a top-up opportunity if you have spare cash. Nothing broken in the long-term thesis.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Another rough day — down 4%, still deeply underwater
watch_today.detail: Pilbara shed another 4% today, closing at $2.64. You're down over 60% on this position. Lithium prices remain depressed with no near-term catalyst. For a long-term investor, the question is whether you still believe in the EV boom timeline. If yes, hold. If that thesis has shifted for you, it's worth reviewing — but don't sell purely on price weakness.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Earnings are out — initial reaction soft but long-term intact
watch_today.detail: Microsoft reported FY27 Q1 results last night and the stock dropped 1.6%. Early analyst reads suggest solid results but not a blowout — cloud and AI revenue still growing. For a long-term holder sitting on a 17.8% gain, this is firmly a hold. No reason to act.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: AI ETF hit by tech sector weakness
watch_today.detail: GXAI fell 2.8% today — the worst ASX mover in your portfolio today. It's tracking global AI stock weakness following Alphabet's disappointing earnings. You're down 15% overall on this one. The AI sector long-term story is unchanged, but expect continued volatility around earnings season. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: Oil spiking — watch for inflation impact
watch_today.detail: Crude oil rose 2.1% last night to $104/barrel, driven by rising Middle East tensions (Strait of Hormuz ship attacks at a yearly high). Higher oil means higher petrol prices and potential inflation pressure — worth watching as it could influence RBA rate decisions in coming months.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision coming — Westpac forecasting a hold
watch_today.detail: The RBA meets next week and Westpac is forecasting rates stay on hold. New RBA Governor Hauser is being described as 'hawkish' (meaning he leans toward keeping rates higher for longer). A hold is mostly priced in, but watch for any surprise language about future cuts — that would move bank stocks and the AUD.

world.summary: The US midterm elections are days away with serious concerns about election integrity and violence. Meanwhile, the Middle East is on edge with fears of a US-Iran war reigniting after the vote, and oil markets are feeling the heat.

stories.title: US election officials brace for violence and intimidation at polling booths
stories.why_it_matters: With the US midterm elections just days away, officials across the country are on high alert for voter intimidation and potential violence at polling booths. A federal judge has already stepped in to order the Trump administration to stop threatening election officials with prosecution — a highly unusual legal intervention. This is about whether American democracy can run a clean vote without intimidation, and the outcome will reshape the balance of power in Congress, which has global ripple effects including on trade, Ukraine aid, and Middle East policy.

stories.title: Middle East on edge — fears Iran war could restart after midterms
stories.why_it_matters: There's growing fear that the US could launch strikes on Iran shortly after the midterm elections, with analysts saying the political calculus changes once votes are counted. Iranian envoys have been meeting Qatari mediators in a last-ditch diplomatic push, while Iran's Supreme Leader Khamenei has publicly warned the US and Israel against any new attacks. Attacks on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz — a critical oil shipping lane — hit their highest level in October since the war began. This is directly behind the oil price spike to $104/barrel you're seeing in markets.

stories.title: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening election officials
stories.why_it_matters: A federal judge has issued a formal order barring the Trump administration from making threats to prosecute state and local election officials. This came after reports that officials in key swing states felt pressured or intimidated ahead of the vote. The court ruling is a significant check on executive power, and signals that the judiciary is actively monitoring attempts to interfere with election administration. It's a reminder that institutional guardrails are being tested in real time.

stories.title: Hormuz ship attacks at yearly high as Middle East tension escalates
stories.why_it_matters: October recorded the highest number of attacks on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz since the Middle East conflict began — a waterway through which about 20% of the world's oil flows. This is a key reason oil prices jumped above $104 last night. If shipping through Hormuz is disrupted further, expect energy prices globally to rise, which would flow through to petrol prices in Australia and add to inflation pressure.

stories.title: Nine voters across the US political spectrum share their views days before the midterms
stories.why_it_matters: The Guardian checked in with nine American voters from across the political divide in the final days of the campaign. The snapshot captures a country deeply divided — with issues like immigration, inflation, abortion rights, and election integrity all featuring prominently. The result will determine whether Trump's Republicans consolidate control of Congress or whether Democrats hold the Senate — a result that shapes US domestic and foreign policy for the next two years.

markets.summary: A rough night on Wall Street last night — Alphabet's disappointing earnings dragged the NASDAQ down nearly 3%, while the S&P 500 fell 1.8%. The ASX held up reasonably well today, edging up 0.18%. Oil jumped over 2% on Middle East tensions, gold pulled back sharply, and the Aussie dollar is steady just above 70 US cents.

politics.summary: Australian politics this weekend centred on RBA interest rate speculation ahead of next week's meeting, a government spending story, and a Federal Court mining decision the government won't appeal.

stories.title: Westpac tips RBA to hold rates next week — but the new governor is hawkish
stories.source: The Motley Fool Australia / The Weekly Times
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia meets next week and Westpac is forecasting rates will stay on hold. But the new RBA Governor, Hauser, is being described as 'hawkish' — meaning he's more inclined to keep rates higher for longer rather than cut quickly. That's relevant for anyone with a mortgage or hoping for rate relief soon. It also matters for growth stocks in your portfolio, as higher rates for longer tend to weigh on tech valuations.

stories.title: Banks sitting on billions in savers' money as interest rates rise
stories.why_it_matters: An ABC investigation has found Australian banks are holding onto billions of dollars in savers' money — benefiting from higher interest rates without fully passing the gains on to deposit holders. As the RBA lifted rates, banks have been pocketing a widening margin between what they charge borrowers and what they pay savers. This is fuelling calls for greater scrutiny of bank profitability and whether consumers are getting a fair deal.

stories.title: Government rules out appealing Federal Court's overturning of McPhillamys mining ban
stories.why_it_matters: The federal government has decided not to appeal a Federal Court decision that overturned a ministerial ban on the McPhillamys gold mine in NSW. The original ban was made under Environment Minister powers, but the court struck it down. By not appealing, the government is effectively letting the mine proceed — a win for the mining company but a blow to environmental groups and local communities who opposed it. It raises questions about the limits of ministerial veto powers over major resource projects.

stories.title: Government spent over $3 million on branded merchandise including condoms and lollies
stories.why_it_matters: A new report reveals the federal government spent more than $3 million on branded merchandise — including condoms, lollies, and other promotional items — as part of government communications and awareness campaigns. Critics are likely to seize on this as wasteful spending, particularly at a time when cost-of-living pressures are squeezing households. It's the kind of spending story that tends to have political legs in the lead-up to an election cycle.

ai.summary: The big AI story this weekend is a rare moment of industry unity — Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Anthropic have all agreed to a new standard letting websites opt out of having their content scraped for AI training. Meanwhile, major AI chatbot services went down simultaneously.

stories.title: Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic agree on AI web-scraping opt-out standard
stories.why_it_matters: In a rare show of unity, all four major AI labs — Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Anthropic — have agreed to support a new technical standard that lets website owners opt out of having their content used to train AI models. Think of it like a 'do not scrape' sign for websites. Previously, AI companies vacuumed up internet content without asking. This is a significant step toward giving publishers, news outlets, and content creators more control over their work — and could reshape how AI models are trained going forward.

stories.title: ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini all went down simultaneously
stories.why_it_matters: The three biggest AI chatbot services — ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini — all experienced outages at the same time over the weekend. For everyday users who've come to rely on these tools for work, writing, or research, simultaneous outages across competing platforms highlights a fragility in the AI ecosystem. It's not clear yet whether these were related or coincidental, but it underscores that even the most powerful AI tools aren't immune to reliability issues.

stories.title: AI safety becomes a political football heading into US midterms
stories.why_it_matters: With the US midterms just days away, AI regulation has become a genuine campaign issue. A left-wing PAC is targeting four House Republicans over their votes on AI oversight legislation, while Senator Elizabeth Warren is attacking Trump's voluntary AI safety deal with tech CEOs as nowhere near enough. The political fight over who controls AI — and how much — is intensifying, and the midterm results could determine whether any binding AI regulations get passed in the US over the next two years.

stories.title: Elizabeth Warren slams Trump's voluntary AI safety deal as insufficient
stories.why_it_matters: Senator Elizabeth Warren has publicly criticised the Trump administration's approach to AI safety, calling a voluntary deal struck between the White House and major tech CEOs 'not nearly enough.' Warren argues that without binding rules, tech companies will self-regulate in their own interests rather than the public's. This debate matters for investors in AI-exposed stocks — tighter regulation could constrain growth, while a voluntary-only framework means fewer restrictions on how companies deploy AI products.

sport.summary: The NRL Grand Final is done — Roosters beat the Knights in a thriller. The Rugby League World Cup is heating up with the Jillaroos making history, and AFL Carlton has landed a big coaching coup.

stories.title: Roosters 19 Knights 18 — Grand Final thriller at Accor Stadium
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters have won the 2026 NRL Premiership, edging out the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in a nail-biting Grand Final at Accor Stadium. Just one point in it at the final siren — it doesn't get closer than that. A heartbreaker for Knights fans and a premiership to savour for Roosters supporters.

stories.title: Jillaroos make history with superstar's six-try haul in RLWC 'massacre'
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian Jillaroos have made incredible history at the Rugby League World Cup, with one player putting on a six-try individual performance in what's being called a 'massacre' of their opponents. The win cements Australia's dominance in the women's game and sets the Jillaroos up as the team to beat as the tournament moves toward the semi-finals.

stories.title: England need a Tongan miracle to keep RLWC semi-final hopes alive
stories.why_it_matters: England's Rugby League World Cup campaign is hanging by a thread — they need Tonga to beat another team for them to have any chance of making the semi-finals. England's own results haven't been enough to secure qualification, so they're now relying on other teams to do them a favour. A nerve-wracking wait for England fans.

stories.title: Nathan Cleary's wildcard NRL option suddenly emerges
stories.why_it_matters: A surprise off-season development is emerging around Penrith halfback Nathan Cleary, with a wildcard NRL option reportedly on the table for Australia's best player. Details are thin, but any movement involving Cleary would reshape the competition's landscape given his standing as arguably the game's top playmaker.

stories.title: Carlton lands premiership-winning AFL coach in major coup
stories.why_it_matters: Carlton has pulled off a major coaching coup, securing a premiership-winning coach to lead the Blues. The club has been rebuilding in recent years and this appointment signals serious ambition — a proven premiership coach joining a club with significant talent is the kind of off-season move that shifts expectations heading into 2027.
